dossier.public_summary: The dip changes strongly between sectors and between individual transits and is not stable even when the same instrument and pipeline are used. This pattern, with depths from ~1400 to ~8100 ppm, is best explained by blended eclipses on different nearby stars rather than a planet on the target. There are neighbours close enough to produce the signal with only a fraction of a percent eclipse.

reasons.why: Depth highly variable between sectors (chi2 44.19 dof 2).
Change persists within same source TESS-SPOC: 1391 ppm (sector 20) vs 7683 ppm (sector 60) vs 8157 ppm (sector 73), not a calibration offset.
Individual transits inconsistent - signal likely not a single fixed planet depth; top 3 transits carry 98% and depths differ strongly.

Flat-bottom shape (v_sigma -3.773) and small size 3.607 Rearth look planet-like with odd_even diff_sigma 0.9517 and secondary snr 2.856, but centroid was inconclusive and a neighbour 52.7 arcsec away needs only 0.26% eclipse to match, supported by the measured depth changes as aperture catches different blends. xgboost planet_rank 0.2 supports non-planet.
